2015|paper-1a|1.question:
A driver turns off the engine after parking his car outdoors under the sun. Two hours later when getting into the car, he feels that the inside of the car is far hotter than outside. The best explanation is

A. the car’s engine is still generating heat after the engine has been switched off.

B. the car’s metal parts absorb infra-red radiation at a faster rate than the surroundings.

C. the glass windows of the car trap infra-red radiation and a greenhouse effect results.

D. the surrounding air is a good insulator of heat which reduces heat loss by conduction.
2015|paper-1a|1.reasoning: Sunlight enters through the glass and warms the interior. The warm interior emits infrared radiation, which the glass transmits poorly, reducing radiative heat loss. This is the greenhouse-effect explanation represented by C.

2015|paper-1a|2.question:
Two objects X and Y are made of the same material. They are heated separately by heaters of the same power. The graph shows the variation of temperature θ of X and Y with time t. What is the ratio of mass of X to that of Y?

A. 3 : 1

B. 2 : 1

C. 1 : 2

D. 2 : 3
2015|paper-1a|2.reasoning: The heaters supply equal energy in the same time. With the same specific heat capacity, mXΔTX = mYΔTY. At the intersection, ΔTX = 60 − 20 = 40 °C and ΔTY = 60 − 40 = 20 °C. Thus mX/mY = 20/40 = 1/2.

2015|paper-1a|3.question:
When an object P is in contact with another object Q, heat flows from P to Q. P must have a higher

(3) specific heat capacity.

A. (1) only

B. (3) only

C. (1) and (2) only

D. (1) and (3) only

2015|paper-1a|4.question:
A particle travels at 2.0 m s−1 due east for 1.5 s and then travels at 4.0 m s−1 due north for 1.0 s. What is the magnitude of its average velocity for the whole journey ?

A. 2.0 m s−1

B. 2.8 m s−1

C. 3.0 m s−1

D. 5.0 m s−1
2015|paper-1a|4.reasoning: Displacement components are 2.0 × 1.5 = 3.0 m east and 4.0 × 1.0 = 4.0 m north. Magnitude of displacement = √(32 + 42) = 5.0 m. Hence |average velocity| = 5.0/(1.5 + 1.0) = 2.0 m s−1. Do not use total distance.

2015|paper-1a|5.question:
A constant net force acting on an object of mass m1 produces an acceleration a1 while the same force acting on another object of mass m2 produces an acceleration a2. If this net force acts on an object of mass (m1 + m2), what would be the acceleration produced?

A. a1 + a2

B. (a1 + a2)/2

C. a1a2/(a1 + a2)

D. 2a1a2/(a1 + a2)
2015|paper-1a|5.reasoning: Newton’s second law gives m1 = F/a1 and m2 = F/a2. Therefore a = F/(m1 + m2) = 1/(1/a1 + 1/a2) = a1a2/(a1 + a2).

2015|paper-1a|6.question:

2015|paper-1b|2.question:
The aqua-lung (a cylinder containing compressed air) for divers has a capacity of 1.0 × 104 cm3. When the aqua-lung is filled, the air inside has a pressure of 210 atm (atmospheric pressure) at 24 °C. The air in the aqua-lung is allowed to expand through a pressure-reducing valve until its pressure equals that of the surrounding water before it is supplied to divers. Assume that the temperature of the air inside the aqua-lung is always equal to that of the surrounding water.

(a) A diver stays in water of temperature 24 °C and pressure 2.0 atm at a depth of 10 m. Find the total volume of air (in cm3) available for the diver from the aqua-lung at this water pressure. (2 marks)

(b) The supply of air in (a) is sufficient for the diver to remain at such a depth for 1 hour.

(b)(i) If the diver breathed in the same volume V0 (in cm3) of air per minute, find V0. (1 mark)

(b)(ii) If the diver dives deeper where the water is of temperature 20 °C and pressure 4.5 atm, estimate how long (in minutes) the air in a fully-filled aqua-lung would last. Assume that the diver breathes in the same volume of air per minute as that found in (b)(i). (3 marks)

(a) At unchanged temperature, p1V1 = p2V2. All the air would occupy V2 = 210(1.0 × 104)/2.0 = 1.05 × 106 cm3 at 2.0 atm. Subtract the 1.0 × 104 cm3 remaining in the cylinder: available volume = 1.04 × 106 cm3.

(b)(i) V0 = (1.04 × 106)/60 ≈ 1.73 × 104 cm3 per minute.

(b)(ii) Use absolute temperatures: T1 = 297 K and T2 = 293 K. From pV/T = constant, the full air supply occupies V = 210(1.0 × 104)(293)/(4.5 × 297) ≈ 4.60 × 105 cm3 at the new conditions.

(b)(ii) Available volume = V − 1.0 × 104 ≈ 4.50 × 105 cm3. Duration = (V − 1.0 × 104)/(1.04 × 106/60) ≈ 26.0 min. Use the unrounded breathing rate.

The official scheme also accepts neglecting the residual cylinder volume: 1.05 × 106 cm3, 1.75 × 104 cm3 per minute, and approximately 26.3 min. Keep the chosen convention consistent.

An acrobat tries to swing from A to C by using a light rope of 8 m long and with one end fixed at point O, which is at the same level as A. He leaves A by holding the end of the rope and then releases it when reaching point B at which the angle between the rope and the vertical is 30°. The acrobat can be treated as a point mass and the rope remains taut and not extended throughout the motion. Neglect air resistance. (g = 9.81 m s−2)

*(b)(ii) Calculate the vertical distance of C below B. (3 marks)

(c) Before reaching the lower platform, is there any change to the acrobat’s mechanical energy among the points A, B and C? (1 mark)

(a) Draw vB tangent to the circular path at B, perpendicular to OB and directed upward to the right, at 30° above the horizontal. The fall in height is 8 cos 30°. Conservation of energy gives ½mvB2 = mg(8 cos 30°), so vB = √(2 × 9.81 × 8 cos 30°) = 11.65896… m s−1 ≈ 11.7 m s−1.

(b)(i) Horizontal velocity is constant after release: x = (vB cos 30°)(1.25) = 12.621… m ≈ 12.6 m.

(b)(ii) Take downward as positive. Initial vertical velocity is −vB sin 30°. Thus the vertical distance below B is y = −(vB sin 30°)(1.25) + ½(9.81)(1.25)2 = 0.3772… m ≈ 0.38 m. Retain the unrounded vB because the two terms nearly cancel.

(c) Mechanical energy is unchanged. Tension does no work because it is perpendicular to motion; after release only gravity does work, exchanging kinetic and gravitational potential energy.
